macro_actions.name: Session-Structuring Actions
macro_actions.description: Organizes the CBT session collaboratively through agenda setting, clinical check-in, homework review, prioritization, summaries, feedback, and assignment of new between-session work.

goal.objective: Create a focused, collaborative, and continuous session structure that connects current work with previous and future therapeutic tasks.

success_levels.ideal: The patient and therapist agree on a clear agenda, review mood and previous homework, prioritize one or two formulation-relevant problems, summarize key learning, exchange feedback, and agree on a specific new homework task.
success_levels.acceptable: The session has a recognizable collaborative structure, although one or more elements are incomplete, brief, or insufficiently linked to the case formulation.
success_levels.unsuccessful: The session is unfocused, therapist-directed, disconnected from previous work, or ends without shared understanding, feedback, or an actionable between-session plan.

goal.reward_hint: The patient can state the agreed agenda, participates in prioritization, understands the session conclusions, and agrees to a clear homework task.

states: Beginning of each CBT session
Several problems compete for attention
The discussion becomes unfocused
Transition between major session topics
End of the session
Continuity with previous or future sessions must be strengthened
included_actions: Prioritization of one or two target problems
macro_actions.delivery_quality_note: Structure should remain collaborative and flexible. Agenda completion should not be treated as rigid adherence when clinically important material emerges and the agenda is revised jointly.

macro_actions.name: Therapeutic Relationship Actions
macro_actions.description: Maintains a collaborative therapeutic relationship through accurate listening, empathy, clarification, shared decision-making, understanding checks, feedback, and rupture repair.

goal.objective: Support a longitudinal therapeutic alliance based on agreement about goals, agreement about therapeutic tasks, and a safe, respectful interpersonal bond.

success_levels.ideal: The patient feels understood and respected, contributes actively to goals and tasks, expresses disagreement or confusion safely, and alliance strains are identified and repaired.
success_levels.acceptable: The relationship is sufficiently collaborative for treatment, but feedback, understanding checks, or repair processes are inconsistent.
success_levels.unsuccessful: The patient feels misunderstood, pressured, excluded, or disengaged, and disagreement or relational strain remains unaddressed.

goal.reward_hint: The patient communicates openly, corrects misunderstandings, contributes to decisions, provides feedback, and remains engaged after disagreement.

states: Throughout all therapy sessions
The patient expresses distress, shame, hesitation, or uncertainty
Goals or therapeutic tasks are being negotiated
The patient appears confused, withdrawn, resistant, or disengaged
Disagreement or an alliance rupture emerges
included_actions: Repairing alliance ruptures when disagreement or disengagement emerges
macro_actions.delivery_quality_note: Alliance should be assessed longitudinally rather than inferred from a single interaction. Evaluation should distinguish goal agreement, task agreement, and interpersonal bond.

macro_actions.name: Cognitive Interventions
macro_actions.description: Helps the patient identify, examine, and modify automatic thoughts, cognitive distortions, intermediate assumptions, and core beliefs through guided discovery.

goal.objective: Increase cognitive awareness and flexibility by helping the patient develop evidence-based, balanced, and personally credible interpretations.

success_levels.ideal: The patient identifies relevant thoughts and beliefs, examines evidence, recognizes distortions, generates balanced alternatives, and reaches conclusions through their own discovery.
success_levels.acceptable: The patient participates in cognitive work and develops partial insight or tentative alternatives with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: The intervention is leading, persuasive, argumentative, disconnected from the formulation, or produces superficial agreement without genuine patient discovery.

goal.reward_hint: The patient states automatic thoughts and beliefs in their own words, evaluates evidence, generates credible alternatives, and shows a meaningful shift in conviction or emotional response.

states: A triggering situation and emotional response have been identified
Automatic thoughts appear linked to distress or maladaptive behavior
Cognitive distortions or rigid beliefs are present
Surface-level cognitive work has not sufficiently explained recurrent patterns
Intermediate assumptions or core beliefs require exploration
included_actions: Examining evidence for and against beliefs
Identification and modification of intermediate assumptions and core beliefs
macro_actions.delivery_quality_note: Competence depends on execution rather than the intervention label alone. Questions should facilitate the patient discovery and must not become leading, persuasive, or coercive.

macro_actions.name: Behavioral Interventions
macro_actions.description: Uses planned activity, behavioral testing, problem solving, exposure-related methods, and skills practice to reduce avoidance and increase adaptive engagement and experiential learning.

goal.objective: Change behavior that maintains the patient difficulties, test formulation-based predictions, increase meaningful activity, and strengthen adaptive skills.

success_levels.ideal: The patient collaboratively undertakes safe, specific, formulation-linked behavioral tasks, reviews predicted versus actual outcomes, and generalizes useful learning.
success_levels.acceptable: The patient attempts relevant activities or skills and obtains partial learning, while barriers and incomplete outcomes are reviewed collaboratively.
success_levels.unsuccessful: The task is imposed, poorly specified, unsafe, unrelated to the formulation, or conducted without adequate review of outcomes and learning.

goal.reward_hint: The patient meaningfully attempts or completes the task, compares expectations with outcomes, identifies learning, and demonstrates increased adaptive engagement.

states: Avoidance, withdrawal, inactivity, or loss of reinforcement maintains the problem
A cognition can be tested through observable behavior
A practical problem or skill deficit interferes with progress
The patient is ready for an appropriately graded behavioral task
A qualified clinician determines that exposure-based treatment is indicated
included_actions: Exposure with response prevention where clinically appropriate
macro_actions.delivery_quality_note: Behavioral tasks should be collaboratively selected, feasible, graded when appropriate, linked to the current formulation, and reviewed for learning rather than judged only by completion.
macro_actions.autonomous_ai_restriction: An AI system must not autonomously conduct real-time exposure or exposure with response prevention. These interventions require clinical judgment and qualified human oversight. AI support should be limited to clinician-approved preparation, documentation, monitoring support, or post-session review.

cross_cutting_principles.formulation_guided_selection: Macro-action selection should be based on the current evolving CBT case formulation rather than selected directly from symptoms alone.
cross_cutting_principles.execution_based_competence: Competence and fidelity depend on how an action is delivered, including collaboration, timing, pacing, non-leading language, responsiveness to patient feedback, and clinical appropriateness.
cross_cutting_principles.human_oversight_boundary: Interventions requiring real-time clinical judgment, particularly exposure-based procedures, must remain under qualified human supervision.
